gaps: Reference counting is name-based over the AST, not type-resolved. An *ast.Ident or selector Sel matching a declaration's bare name is counted as a reference to it. Where distinct_definitions_for_name > 1, external_refs is an UPPER BOUND and may attribute another symbol's call sites to this record. Downstream consumers must treat name_ambiguous records as unreliable counts.

Selector expressions are counted by their Sel name, so `x.Foo` counts toward every top-level `Foo` in the tree. This most affects methods and short names (Name, ID, Get, New, Service, Value, Error, String, Client, Config). It is directional evidence, not proof.

Struct field names, interface method names, function parameters, and locally declared identifiers are excluded from the ref index (their declaration positions are masked), but a *use* of a field named the same as a top-level symbol is still counted.

external_refs counts references from any file outside the DEFINING DIRECTORY. In-package references (including in-package _test.go files) are deliberately excluded and are NOT reported; a 0 here is not a claim of deadness — mechanisms 1-9 in the preamble are unresolved for every record in this map and must be resolved per-symbol by a later phase.

Interface satisfaction (mechanism 1), functional options (2), struct embedding (3), serialization tags (4), //go:embed (5), init() side effects (8), and reflection / string-keyed lookup / string-built SQL (9) are NOT resolved by this map. A method reachable only through an interface value is counted here only when the interface's method name matches, and a symbol referenced only from a string literal or a struct tag has zero refs in this map by construction.
registration_sites is a path heuristic, not a wiring analysis: refs under cmd/, internal/adapters/scheduler/, or in a file named routes.go / router.go. It does not read the DI graph.

Blank identifier declarations (`_`) are enumerated as declaration positions but emitted as no record; blank-import interface assertions such as `var _ Iface = (*T)(nil)` therefore contribute refs to the interface and type but produce no record of their own.
Files that failed to parse (if any) are reported on stderr by the generator; the run that produced this map reported none.
Both build-tag universes are covered: parsing ignores build constraints, so integration-tagged files are parsed and their refs are segregated into integration_refs rather than dropped.
ref_sites and integration_refs are capped at 10 entries each per record; external_refs is the authoritative count and the arrays are samples. Truncation is stated in the record's note.
Generic type parameters are masked as declarations but their uses count toward same-named top-level symbols.

Enumeration fact, no conclusion drawn: `internal/domain/storage` is one of the 48 packages but contributes ZERO records — its only tracked file is doc.go, which holds a package comment and no top-level declaration (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> -- internal/domain/storage` returns only `internal/domain/storage/doc.go`). A later phase should decide what, if anything, that means.

`internal/integration` contributes records but is NOT one of the 48 packages under the baseline definition, because every tracked .go file in it is a _test.go file. The 48-package total and the set of directories appearing in defined_at therefore differ by exactly these two entries (storage out, integration in) and both differences are explained above.
